_about: Parameters of the household travel survey design and of the SYNTHETIC respondent file (stm/survey.py). No survey was carried out. Same labels as config/model.json; SYNTHETIC marks a value that only shapes simulated respondents.

target_margin_mode_share.label: ASSUMPTION
target_margin_mode_share.note: half-width of the confidence interval of the car share of commuters in each region: 2.5 percentage points

target_relative_margin_trip_rate.label: ASSUMPTION
target_relative_margin_trip_rate.note: half-width of the confidence interval of commuting trips per resident per weekday in each region, as a share of the estimate

strata.label: ASSUMPTION
strata.note: households are drawn with equal probability within a region, so the expected sample of a subzone is proportional to its households

persons_per_household.label: ASSUMPTION
persons_per_household.note: the same value as scenario_2030.persons_per_home in config/model.json; turns Census residents into a household frame

household_size_distribution.label: ASSUMPTION
household_size_distribution.note: probabilities of households of 1 to 6 persons, mean 3.1; not taken from a Census table. Used for the design effect, where the cluster size that matters is E[m^2] / E[m], and to build the synthetic households

intra_household_correlation.label: ASSUMPTION
intra_household_correlation.note: correlation of commuting mode between two commuters of one household, used in the design effect 1 + (m - 1) rho, also applied to the trip rate; no source

expected_response_rate.label: ASSUMPTION
expected_response_rate.note: share of issued households expected to complete the survey; no source

allocation.label: ASSUMPTION
allocation.note: each region gets the sample that meets both precision targets; proportional allocation of the same total is reported for comparison

seed.label: SYNTHETIC
seed.note: seed of the saved respondent file; replicate r of the repeated-sampling check uses seed + r

replicates.label: SYNTHETIC
replicates.note: independent synthetic surveys drawn to measure bias, root mean square error and confidence-interval coverage

mode_copy_probability.label: SYNTHETIC
mode_copy_probability.note: probability that a commuter's mode is drawn with the household's random number instead of the commuter's own; two commuters of one household then share their draw with probability 0.55 squared, about 0.30

response_intercept.label: SYNTHETIC
response_intercept.note: logit of a household's response probability: intercept

response_private_housing.label: SYNTHETIC
response_private_housing.note: added for households in condominiums and landed housing (harder to reach)

response_central_region.label: SYNTHETIC
response_central_region.note: added for households in the Central Region

response_no_resident_outside_working_age.label: SYNTHETIC
response_no_resident_outside_working_age.note: added when every member is aged 20-64 (nobody at home in the daytime)

response_per_car_commuter.label: SYNTHETIC
response_per_car_commuter.note: added for each member who commutes by car. This is the part of non-response that depends on the answer itself and that no census margin describes

margins.label: REAL
margins.note: Census of Population 2020 residents by subzone, age group and type of dwelling (SingStat Table Builder 17560 and 17562), already in data/inputs/

raking_tolerance.label: ASSUMPTION
raking_tolerance.note: largest relative difference between a weighted margin and its census total at which raking stops
